answer: Because the canyon index resolves every citation against the summit checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the spiral audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 297 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 297 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A farm of 4911 identities would post 2821 proofs and burn roughly 86 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
